title: SIEM connector throttling, privacy & field redaction spec
content:
Purpose and scope:
This is a working-spec for SIEM export connectors focusing on three cross-cutting concerns that repeatedly cause customer friction: (1) per-tenant throttling and backpressure handling, (2) field-level privacy (redaction/pseudonymization) and retention constraints, and (3) compatibility hints for Splunk HEC, Datadog Logs API, and Azure Sentinel ingestion (Log Analytics Data Collector).

Context / why this doc exists:
- Lots of customers ask for SIEM export but have strict PII rules or rate limits on their SIEM ingestion endpoints.
- Existing connector specs assume full-fidelity events; we need a reproducible approach for safe exports, deterministic pseudonymization, and graceful degradation when a customer's SIEM is constrained.
- This is intended to be referenced by Solutions Eng, Security, and the Connector devs in serving/runtime and private deployments.

High-level principles:
- Do no leak PII by default: exports must pass a redaction policy unless customer explicitly opts into full-event export in a signed contract.
- Deterministic pseudonymization: where identifiers are needed for correlation, use HMAC-based pseudonymization with per-customer keys so correlation = possible but reidentification = infeasible without key material.
- Fail closed on privacy, fail open on availability: if redaction rules can't be applied due to an error, drop the event and emit an audit/error metric. If the SIEM endpoint rejects due to rate-limits, backpressure + graceful sampling is allowed with telemetry.
- Minimal required fields: standardized audit envelope to ensure downstream dashboards work across SIEMs.

Audit/event envelope (required fields for all connectors)
Note: this is intentionally small to maximize compatibility. All connectors MUST include these top-level keys (use these exact names in the exported JSON).
- event_id: string (uuid4)
- ts: ISO-8601 timestamp (UTC)
- tenant_id: string (customer id)
- source: string (redwood-service-name, e.g., inference-api)
- event_type: string (e.g., auth.authentication_success, model.infer_request)
- actor: string|null (pseudonymized user id or system actor)
- resource: string|null (resource id / model id / route)
- outcome: string (success | failure | throttled)
- severity: string (info | warning | error | critical)
- payload: object (freeform - see field mapping guidance below)

Audit schema guidance / RBAC v2 fields
- rbac_role: string (role name from RBAC v2; e.g., admin, org_admin, org_viewer, service_token)
- rbac_action: string (API verb or permission key)
- rbac_target: string (resource type + id)
- session_id: optional string
- request_id: optional string
These should be included in payload if available. For private deployments we expect full RBAC traces; for hosted exports we will include what we have.

Field-level privacy & redaction rules (recommended default)
Categories to redact by default (unless customer allows): email, phone, ip_address, raw_prompt_text, credit_card, ssn, user_display_name, user_email, client_cert_subject
Strategy table (high level):
- email, phone, ssn, credit_card: REMOVE or REPLACE with token string "[REDACTED]" unless customer asked for pseudonymization.
- ip_address: HASH(ip_address) using HMAC-SHA256(customer_key, ip) and store as hex-sha256 prefix (first 16 chars) to support correlation without exposing IP.
- user ids (actor): PSEUDONYMIZE via HMAC-SHA256(customer_key, user_id) with a stable prefix like "uid_" + hex.
- raw_prompt_text / generation text: by default REMOVE; if customer signs full-data addendum, allow truncated prompt (first 128 chars) + hash.
- model logits/attention/embedding vectors: NEVER include in SIEM exports. These are considered high-sensitivity.

Implementation notes for redaction/pseudonymization:
- Use a per-tenant key stored in KMS; connector reads key via Config + KMS API. The HMAC key SHOULD NOT be exported to customer.
- Deterministic output: HMAC-based pseudonymization enables cross-event correlation inside customer's SIEM while preventing easy reidentification.
- Regex heuristics: keep them simple and well-logged. Example regex patterns we use internally (not exhaustive): email: "[A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Za-z0-9.-]+\.[A-Za-z]{2,}" ; ip v4: "\b(?:\d{1,3}\\.){3}\d{1,3}\b"
- Redaction errors: if regex or transform fails, emit metric redaction_errors and route event to a quarantine queue for manual review.

Connector-specific notes
1) Splunk HEC
- Preferred payload: event envelope as JSON in the "event" field (standard HEC). Use HEC token authentication.
- Batch guidance: prefer 1–500 events per batch; keep payload size < 5MB.
- Default max throughput: suggest customer limit of 2000 events/sec per token; enable per-token soft_limit and hard_limit.
- Retry policy: exponential backoff with jitter, max_retries=5, drop after final failure and increment dropped_events with reason.
- Special header: add X-Redwood-Export-Version: 1.1 and X-Redwood-Tenant: <tenant_id> so customer parsers can route.

2) Datadog Logs API
- Datadog allows event-level attributes and structured logs. Send JSON as per Datadog Logs ingest (api.datadoghq.com/v1/input).
- Rate guidance: customers frequently set per-api-key rate limits; default safe target = 1k events/sec. Use batching to keep under limits.
- Fields: map envelope.event_type -> dd.sourcecategory, envelope.severity -> dd.level, tenant_id -> dd.tags:tenant:<id>.
- If using Datadog rehydration features, include dd.trace_id if available.

3) Azure Sentinel / Log Analytics (Data Collector API)
- Use per-workspace shared key + custom log type. Payloads are POSTed as an array of JSON objects (max 30MB per post).
- Batch guidance: 1–10k records per batch depending on record size; recommend max 50k small-records/min. Throttling is common; monitor HTTP 429 and use backoff.
- Field mapping: resource -> LogType, tenant_id -> CustomerId (custom field).

Throttling, backpressure, sampling and graceful degradation
- Components involved: connector output queue (in memory/durable), per-tenant token bucket, delivery workers.
- Token bucket per-tenant default: rate=1000 tokens/sec, burst=2000. Values overrideable per customer via dedicated config.
- When the token bucket is empty: connector must apply one of the following strategies (configurable per-tenant):
  * queue-and-block (for Dedicated/private installs with adequate storage)
  * drop-low-priority (samples non-critical events, e.g., model.metrics)
  * sample-1-in-N (fall back to deterministic sampling by event_type)
  * escalate-to-customer (emit alert to customer contacts + pause exports)
- Backpressure signal to upstream: when queue_depth > 80% for >30s, emit backpressure=true to internal router so upstream can reduce event generation rate where supported. This requires coordination with serving/runtime teams (JIRA: RUNTIME-2379).
- Circuit breaker thresholds: close connector (stop sending) after 5 consecutive 5xx responses or 30% HTTP 429 across 2 minutes, whichever first. Auto-retry/repair window = 5m.

Batching & serialization recommendations
- Always compress batches with gzip; set Content-Encoding: gzip. This reduces costs and keeps payloads under SIEM limits.
- Include a small batch metadata header structure: batch_id, batch_ts, tenant_id, event_count. This is helpful for customer debugging and replay.

Monitoring and telemetry (metrics & logs)
Emit the following metrics (export to Redwood monitoring + included in the connector monitoring stream):
- siem.events.sent (counter)
- siem.events.dropped (counter) with tag reason:{throttled,redaction_error,serialization_error,customer_reject} 
- siem.retry.count (counter)
- siem.backpressure.activated (gauge 0/1)
- siem.queue.depth (gauge)
- siem.avg_latency_ms (histogram)
- siem.redaction.errors (counter)
- siem.pseudonymization.key_errors (counter)
Recommended alert thresholds (initial):
- siem.events.dropped > 100/min => pager (investigate customer-side rejects or connector regressions)
- siem.backpressure.activated == 1 for > 5m => page SRE and SE assigned to the customer
- siem.redaction.errors > 10/day => warn team; possible KMS or pattern regression

Customer onboarding checklist (what Solutions Eng needs from customer)
- Which SIEM(s) and exact ingestion endpoints (HEC URL / Datadog API key / Azure workspace ID + shared key)
- Ingestion throughput requirements (peak eps) and acceptable latency/SLA (eg: 95% events < 1m)
- PII policy: list of fields that absolutely must be removed vs permitted with pseudonymization vs allowed in full
- IP allowlist / egress config (if customer restricts inbound IPs)
- Retention & deletion: customer retention period and confirmation mechanism for deletion requests
- Contact list for export failures and backpressure events

Connector config knobs (exposed to SE & customer as needed)
- redaction_mode: strict | pseudonymize | none (default: strict)
- pseudonymization_algorithm: hmac-sha256
- batch_max_events: integer
- batch_max_bytes: integer
- token_bucket_rate, token_bucket_burst
- backpressure_strategy: queue-and-block | drop-low-priority | sample-1-in-N | escalate
- kms_key_ref: string (KMS URI)

Evidence automation and audit trail
- For every exported batch, create a minimal export-audit record stored in Redwood's audit-index (not in the customer's SIEM) with: batch_id, tenant_id, exported_event_count, redaction_summary (counts per redaction type), export_status. This enables compliance teams to validate exports and respond to deletion requests without rehydrating full events.
- Evidence artifacts for audits: signed manifest files with SHA256 of batch payload (post-redaction), export time, and KMS key_id used. Store manifests in internal S3 with standard retention.

Operational playbook (short)
- On 429 spikes: check queue_depth, inspect batch rejection body, increase batching temporarily (if allowed) and enable backoff. If > 10m, notify customer and SRE.
- On persistent 5xx: circuit breaker -> pause -> redeploy path with fallback to alternate endpoint if configured.
- On redaction errors: route failing event to quarantine, emit siem.redaction.errors, open a short-lived internal ticket and notify privacy SME.

Customer-facing considerations & contract language notes (draft wording)
- By default Redwood will apply automated redaction to exported events. Customers who require full fidelity logs must sign a Full-Export Addendum (FEA) and provide a documented PII acceptance plan.
- Customers are responsible for their SIEM ingestion limits, firewall rules that permit Redwood export IPs, and API keys/secrets. Redwood will provide recommended rate budgets and best-effort retries; not guaranteeing delivery if customer endpoint rejects due to capacity (unless under dedicated/reserved contract).

Examples (snippets)
- Splunk HEC event envelope example (post-redaction):
  {
    "time": "2025-02-18T15:12:03Z",
    "host": "redwood-inference",
    "event": { "event_id": "9b7f2b14-...", "ts": "2025-02-18T15:12:02Z", "tenant_id": "acme-corp", "event_type": "model.infer_request", "actor": "uid_3f9a2b", "outcome": "success", "payload": { "model": "gpt-small-quant" } }
  }

- Pseudonymization example (pseudo): HMAC-SHA256(key, "user:12345") -> "uid_3f9a2b..."

Open questions / TODOs
- Should we allow customers to supply their own pseudonymization salt? (JIRA: SEC-5142)
- What is the canonical list of regexes for redaction and who maintains them? (owner: privacy-team)
- How do we expose per-tenant backpressure signals to the serving runtime in hosted mode without leaking tenant metadata across shards? (RUNTIME-2379)
- Add integration test harness for each SIEM that simulates 429/5xx, content-filtering, and verifies metrics.

Notes to implementer (quick dev checklist)
- Add HMAC helper + KMS fetch flow (unit tests for deterministic output)
- Implement token-bucket middleware per-tenant (configurable)
- Add quarantine queue + review tooling for redaction failures
- Implement metrics and wiring to Redwood monitoring and customer-visible export metrics

Slack bookmarks / references:
- #sec-ingest pinned messages: KMS key rotation schedule, export-ip ranges
- Confluence: /display/SEC/SIEM+Export+Guidelines (linked_artifacts above)

End of doc (working). This file is deliberately practical and implementation-oriented — aim to convert into a formal Connector Spec and a shorter Customer Onboarding checklist for final publication.
